scope: Theorem 5.1 (Sharp connected bounds) of the manuscript “Hard-sphere fluctuations on the regular Boltzmann lifespan” (preprints/Hard-sphere-fluctuations-on-the-regular-Boltzmann-lifespan-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 364 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 e294d8e5097f8d0e), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 25. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Choose the parameters Γ, L as in Theorem 4.9, increasing L, if necessary, by an amount depending only on the uniform bounds for the Boltzmann solution and on T. This one choice works for every fixed factorial order and every fixed bounded observation list. For each fixed h, ∥cϵ h∥TV ≤ Chµ1−h . (5.2) For h = 1, 2, the measures µh−1cϵ h converge against bounded continuous record tests to the signed sums of the retained global trees with trivial initial cumulants. At a contact their weight is the incoming flux [(v − v∗) · ω]+ dt dω; a scattering contact has sign +1, and a non-scattering contact has sign −1. The independent birth factors are fiτ . The sums of the absolute retained diagram measures, after multiplication by µh−1, are bounded uniformly with a sufficiently small Gaussian weight in their designated endpoint velocities. The same bound holds for the limiting tree measures, and for the Gaussian weights in finitely many retained record velocities after decreasing the exponent. Among the retained connected diagrams, the sum of the absolute measures having a nontrivial initial cumulant or a global cycle is o(µ1−h). The assertions about Gaussian weights concern retained diagrams and their limits; no weighted estimate for a microscopic expansion remainder is asserted.
